subject: How does the adaptation of the diagonal metric work?

messages.author: 28e4cea0c0378ed9
messages.subject: How does the adaptation of the diagonal metric work?
parts:
Dear Stan developers,

A general question; could anyone tell me how the joint adaptation of the step length parameter and the diagonal metric for NUTS in stan work. Hoffman and Gelman's original paper on NUTS
gives an excellent description on how the step length parameter is chosen under for a fixed mass matrix. However, I assume that adapting both mass matrix and step length jointly would
require some kind of modification of the adaptation algorithm?

Regards, Tore Selland Kleppe

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How does the adaptation of the diagonal metric work?
parts:
We need to write this up better for the manual.
Michael, if you respond to this, I can shovel it into the
manual.

The best description we currently have is in the 2.2.0
in the description of the command-line options under
the heading:

Sampling Adaptation-Specific Parameters

The sketchy answer is that for the mass matrix, we use
penalized maximum likelihood estimates of the (co)variance
of the parameters found in the warmup iterations. It's
blocked so that we always try to use the second-half of
the warmup iterations.

The step size is still estimated with dual averaging.
I believe it gets re-estimated from scratch after the
update of the mass matrix at the end of each block.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How does the adaptation of the diagonal metric work?
parts:
As Bob noted the adaptation procedure is discussed in the manual.

Warmup is separated into multiple “slow” and “fast” phases. In
a fast phases only the step size is adapted, while in the slow phases
both the step size and the metric are adapted. More specifically,
in a slow phase the step size is dynamically optimized with dual
averaging while the sample covariance is aggregated and at the
end of the slow phase the sample covariance is used to update
the metric.

Currently warmup begins with a fast phase meant to find high
probability mass. A series of expanding slow phases then
learn the metric before a final fast phase makes final tweaks
to the step size after the last update to the metric.
